chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Jesse Price replaces Bill Beeson
summary: After a bus quarrel with Ella, Moe Gale's office hired Kansas City drummer Jesse Price, a near copy of Chick, who joined for the western tour.

bands.name: Ella Fitzgerald and Her Famous Orchestra

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What about the theater in Kansas City?

Oh, we go into Kansas City. We had played St. Louis. And it's an amazing thing. Ella was so popular -- the band was going over so big, you know. And Bill Beeson was still with the band. We did good in Chicago. We had a good show. We had -- Buck and Bubbles was with us. And some other people I can't recall. But we always had a good show -- really good show. Peg Leg Bates was one of the stars with us at one time. He always travelled with us, you know. In California, we had Buck and Bubbles, Nicholas Kids -- oh! Well you know what Ella did and what Taft was doing and the band, you know. We had a terrific show in Chicago. I mean the show was outstanding. They broke all records out there. But before we got to California, we was
travelling through -- we had to go into St. Louis. From St. Louis into Kansas City.
So after we left St. Louis, the road manager travelled with us. He come back to me and say, "You know you're going to pick up a new drummer."
Who was that?
Frenchie -- a guy called Frenchie who worked for Moe Gale. He was a road manager. We called him Frenchie.
Frenchie says, "Can I talk to you for a minute?"
"Yeah."
He says, "You know, before we leave here tonight, I want to tell you something."
"Okay." We were still in St. Louis.
He called me over to the side -- he said, "You know, we're going to pick up a new drummer in Kansas City."
"A new drummer?" I say, "Why?"
"Well you know, you heard about the argument on the bus (inaudible) with Beeson and Ella. You know, they got into a little argument on the bus (inaudible)."

Beeson said something to Ella and Ella said, 'Well, you can go home if you want to,' you know.
So that was a couple of days before we had to play (inaudible).
So they knew of the drummer. In fact, I knew of one in Kansas City. But I didn't think he would leave because he was teaching in Kansas City.
He was working a big music store -- like Manny's -- one of the big stores in Kansas City that sold drums and everything.
He was a teacher there, you know.
This was Jesse Price.
Yeah. He was teaching there. So Jesse Price agreed -- Moe Gale must've made him a good offer and he agreed to join the band when we got there.
And we didn't rehearse with him. He just came down to the date that we played in Kansas City.
And he just stood on the side and watch everything that went down. He didn't play anything
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
with us that night.
Beeson was still playing.
Beeson was still playing.
He just stood on the side and watched everything we were doing.
Now --
See, when I met him in Kansas City after the date, I sat down and I talked to him.
I told him to go through the whole book, you know, (inaudible). And the next -- I forget the next (inaudible) time we played. We was going to to Salt Lake --
You know, we was going on out (inaudible).
See, by the time we got to California, he was well rehearsed, because he knew everything was going down. We went over the songs.
Because we used to have a habit of doing the show -- doing like before intermission, we would do like a little forty-five minute show.
People would stand around and watch, you know, stop dancing -- watch the band put on a show.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
We would do a real fast one you couldn't dance to and {feature (inaudible)} the drummer and things, like that.
We tried him out on a couple of things, and he came through with flying colors. He was the carbon copy of Chick Webb. Fast wrist, fast feet, {inaudible} everything.
Handle the hi-hat cymbals -- he was on everything. He was an all around drummer. He was something else.
When we got to California, he was just like -- like he had been with the band for about ten years, you know.
He was just like glued in there. He just -- you know, because he had -- in fact, I think he was an idol of Chick.
And he had been listening to Chick's records and everything, because he knew everything that we did, you know.
When we got to California, there was nothing you had to tell this man. This man was just sensational on stage.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
This was Moe Gale's decision or Ella's decision?
That came from the office. I didn't know anything about it until the day before I got to Kansas City.
I met him the day -- the night -- the next day I met him he came over to the hotel and we played that date that night, and he just stood there on the side and watched us.
He'd sit up in the back of the bandstand. Beeson never met him. Beeson knew he was going to leave that night, and I think Beeson met him at intermission or something.
I never knew Jesse Price so I never met him. But he was the thing that really saved the day for us out there, because we were playing some real heavy dates.
We needed a drummer like that. We could go back and do some of the heavy things that Chick Webb did, you know.
He could do them. He did them fine. And when we got to -- we played at --
